question: Triangle \(ABC\) with \(AB = 50\) and \(AC = 10\) has area \(120.\) Let \(D\) be the midpoint of \(\overline{AB},\) and let \(E\) be the midpoint of \(\overline{AC}.\) The angle bisector of \(\angle BAC\) intersects \(\overline{DE}\) and \(\overline{BC}\) at \(F\) and \(G,\) respectively. What is the area of quadrilateral \(FDBG?\)
solution:
The angle bisector divides both \(DE\) and \(BC\) in the same ratio, which will let us compare two trapezoid areas. Write \([P]\) for the area of figure \(P\).

Since \(D\) and \(E\) are midpoints, \(AD=25\), \(AE=5\), and \(DE\parallel BC\). Applying the Angle Bisector Theorem in triangles \(ADE\) and \(ABC\) gives
\[
\frac{DF}{FE}=\frac{AD}{AE}=5,
\qquad
\frac{BG}{GC}=\frac{AB}{AC}=5.
\]
Each divided side therefore has six equal ratio parts, five of which belong to the segment nearer \(B\). Hence
\[
DF=\frac56DE,
\qquad
BG=\frac56BC.
\]
The trapezoids \(FDBG\) and \(EDBC\) lie between the same parallel lines \(DE\) and \(BC\), so they have the same height. Using the trapezoid area formula,
\[
\frac{[FDBG]}{[EDBC]}
=\frac{DF+BG}{DE+BC}
=\frac56.
\]
Also, \(\triangle ADE\) is similar to \(\triangle ABC\) with side-length ratio \(\frac12\), so its area is
\[
[ADE]=\left(\frac12\right)^2\!\cdot120=30.
\]
Thus \([EDBC]=120-30=90\), and
\[
[FDBG]=\frac56\cdot90=\boxed{75}.
\]
The answer is choice D.
